subject.title: [Bug]: restart storm from telegram.retry.jitter type mismatch + misleading doctor SecretRef for Telegram token

question: After the linked jitter-migration PR is resolved, should the remaining SecretRef, CDP profile-lock, and multi-state-root diagnostics stay in this umbrella issue or be split into narrower issues?
rationale: The central crash-loop branch has a concrete open PR, but the rest spans credential diagnostics, browser/CDP service isolation, and operator recovery UX; choosing the permanent tracking shape needs maintainer ownership and security/product judgment.

options.title: Land jitter, then split leftovers
options.body: Use the linked PR for the boolean jitter repair, then create or reuse narrow issues for any still-reproducible SecretRef and CDP/service branches before closing this umbrella issue.

options.title: Keep this as the umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers verify all branches together, accepting that one broad report will continue to block cleanup.

options.title: Close after jitter only
options.body: Close once the linked jitter PR lands and ask reporters to open fresh issues for remaining branches, risking loss of the existing SecretRef/CDP context.

recommendation.title: Land jitter, then split leftovers
recommendation.body: Use the linked PR for the boolean jitter repair, then create or reuse narrow issues for any still-reproducible SecretRef and CDP/service branches before closing this umbrella issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has recent history on the doctor/config-flow layer that controls the central migration path and can route whether the remaining branches should split.
